description: STRENGTHENING GUAM DPHSS INFRASTRUCTURE, WORKFORCE, AND DATA SYSTEMS - OVER THE COURSE OF THE LAST FEW YEARS, THREE EMERGENCY DECLARATIONS STRAINED GUAM’S DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC HEALTH AND SOCIAL SERVICES INFRASTRUCTURE. THE FIRST STATE OF EMERGENCY WAS DECLARED IN 2019 WHEN GUAM'S LOCALLY ACQUIRED DENGUE FEVER CASE WAS IDENTIFIED, PROMPTING DPHSS TO TAKE IMMEDIATE ACTION TO CONTAIN AND EDUCATE THE ISLAND OF GUAM ON HOW TO MINIMIZE THE SPREAD OF THE VIRUS. TWO MONTHS LATER IN NOVEMBER 2019, DPHSS WAS IN ANOTHER STATE OF EMERGENCY AS THE MAIN PUBLIC HEALTH FACILITY EXPERIENCED AN ELECTRICAL FIRE RESULTING IN THE BUILDING BEING DEEMED UNSAFE FOR UTILIZATION OF CRUCIAL DPHSS PROGRAMS AND SERVICES.  MOST PROGRAMS AND DIVISIONS HOUSED IN THE CENTRAL FACILITY HAD TO ABRUPTLY RELOCATE TO VARIOUS LOCATIONS THROUGHOUT THE ISLAND. IN MARCH 2020, THE FIRST POSITIVE COVID-19 CASE WAS IDENTIFIED AND DPHSS LED AND CONTINUES TO LEAD THE ISLAND-WIDE RESPONSE EFFORT BY PLANNING AND OPENING TESTING AND VACCINATION SITES, LAUNCHING EDUCATIONAL CAMPAIGNS ABOUT HOW TO REDUCE THE SPREAD OF THE VIRUS, AND COLLECTING COVID-19 RELATED DATA TO BE SHARED WITH STAKEHOLDERS ON THE STATE OF THE ISLAND.  THE PANDEMIC HIGHLIGHTED EXISTING CHALLENGES AND INTRODUCED NEW DIFFICULTIES TO DPHSS RELATING TO WORKFORCE AND DATA IMPROVEMENTS WHICH RESULTED IN DPHSS’ COVID-19 PANDEMIC RESPONSE ACTIVITIES MORE ARDUOUS AND LESS EFFICIENT IN NATURE. THE LAST FEW YEARS HAVE HIGHLIGHTED THE NEED FOR A ROBUST PUBLIC HEALTH INFRASTRUCTURE TO ENSURE DPHSS IS PREPARED TO RESPOND TO EMERGING THREATS. THIS CAN BE ACHIEVED BY INCREASING THE SIZE AND CAPABILITY OF DPHSS’ WORKFORCE, HAVING A STRONGER PUBLIC HEALTH FOUNDATIONAL CAPABILITY, AND UTILIZING A MORE MODERN AND EFFICIENT DATA SYSTEM. THESE GOALS WILL ULTIMATELY ADVANCE THE QUALITY AND PERFORMANCE DPHSS PROVIDE TO ITS CONSTITUENTS, THE ISLAND OF GUAM.

cfda_info.cfda_objectives: The purpose of the Emerging Infections Programs (EIP) is to assist in local, state, and national efforts to prevent, control, and monitor the public health impact of infectious diseases. The EIP cooperative agreement was formed in 1995 as a key component of CDC’s national strategy to address and reduce emerging infectious disease (EID) threats.  The EIP is a population-based network of state health agencies and their collaborators, including (but not limited to) academic institutions, local health departments, public health and clinical laboratories, infection control professionals, and healthcare providers.   The unique strength of the EIP lies in the network’s ability to quickly translate surveillance and research activities into informed policy and public health practice.

cfda_info.cfda_objectives: The intent of this program is to fund state, local, and territorial public health departments for HHS Secretarial declared and non-declared public health emergencies having an overwhelming impact on jurisdictional resources. These emergencies require federal support to effectively respond to, manage, and address a significant public health threat. CDC seeks to enhance the Nation’s ability to rapidly mobilize and respond to specific public health crises or emergencies. In addition to immediate response activities, this program provides a mechanism to accelerate readiness for an impending infectious disease threat or other public health crises identified on the event horizon.
